newsitem.title: UK: Gold steadies, wheat and oil mark time.
newsitem.headline: Gold steadies, wheat and oil mark time.

text.p: A slide in the price of gold was braked on Tuesday although dealers said the respite may not last long, while commodity markets also saw oil and wheat fail to extend Monday rallies.
A speculator sell-off on a view that gold is not an attractive bet at current values has taken it down by some $10 per ounce since the last trading day of 1996.
But a London close on Tuesday at $359.35 was $1.40 up from Monday on a short covering bounce.
"Most people are very sceptical about how long it will last," said a London dealer.
Demand for heating fuel in the present cold northern winter continued to support high oil prices but the benchmark Brent Blend of crude was little changed from Monday at around $24.50 per barrel.
Wheat prices on the Chicago Board of Trade for the March futures contract were also just easier from Monday's best values, at around $3.90 per bushel.
The price of Robusta coffee beans sank close to levels below $1,200 a tonne that had prevailed before a 1994 frost in Brazil, followed by drought, caused a spectacular rally and it quadrupled.

The steady erosion was arrested on Tuesday by news that Brazil, according to an official there, is working on the basis that it may have a 1997/98 crop below 20 million 60-kilo bags -- at the low end of forecasts.

London March Robusta futures ended up $18 per tonne at $1,230 after a low of $1,203. Base metals on the London Metal Exchange (LME) were mostly just firmer after flagship copper held up well despite a build in LME-supervised warehouse stocks of almost 11,500 tonnes. Most of that went into Singapore, from where it is unlikely to move to alleviate tightness in the West.

Copper finished the afternoon LME session firmer at $2,221 per tonne, above $2,215 technical resistance. Nickel extended a rally based on short covering to end at a firm $7,080 per tonne. Some key prices at 1715 GMT on Tuesday -
